description: Create the complete NAS100 signal bot project structure with all core modules - data fetching, edge detection, signal generation, Kelly criterion math, confluence scoring, Telegram alerts, and scheduling. This is the main implementation feature.
steps: Create requirements.txt with dependencies: yfinance, pandas, numpy, python-telegram-bot, schedule, pyyaml, ta (technical analysis library), pytz, pytest (dev)

Create config.example.yaml with all user-configurable settings: telegram_bot_token, telegram_chat_id, account_balance (for Kelly sizing suggestions), default_risk_percent, max_kelly_fraction, ticker symbol (^NDX or NQ=F), check_intervals (market_open, after_first_hour, kill_zone, afternoon), timezone (US/Eastern)
Create nas100bot/config.py - loads YAML config, validates required fields, provides defaults

Create nas100bot/data.py - fetches NAS100 data via yfinance: daily bars (for multi-day setups), hourly/1h bars (for intraday setups like first candle), calculates Previous Day High (PDH), Previous Day Low (PDL), ATR, RSI(14). Caches data to avoid re-fetching.

Create nas100bot/edges.py - implements all edge detection functions from the research. LONG edges: (1) first_1h_candle_bullish (>+0.3% close, 87.6% WR), (2) pdl_sweep_reclaim (PDL sweep >0.3R + close back above, 76.4% WR), (3) rsi_oversold (RSI14 daily <30, 70.1% WR on 5-day hold, avg +1.36%), (4) consecutive_red_days (5 red days, 63.4% bounce, avg +0.50%), (5) rolling_decline (5-day decline >5%, 67.3% WR, avg +1.44%), (6) large_drop_bounce (single day >4% drop, 66.7% next day green, avg +0.59%). SHORT edges: (1) first_1h_candle_bearish (<-0.3% close, 84.8% WR), (2) pdh_sweep_rejection (PDH sweep >0.2R + close back below, 83.1% WR), (3) large_rally_fade (>3% single-day rally, 58.5% next day red, avg -0.73%), (4) weak_period_short (Thu/Fri 3PM ET, 46-47% green rate). Each edge function returns: triggered (bool), win_rate, avg_win, avg_loss, sample_size, description.

Create nas100bot/kelly.py - implements Kelly criterion: kelly_fraction = (win_rate * avg_win - (1-win_rate) * avg_loss) / avg_win. Also compute expected_value = (win_rate * avg_win) - ((1-win_rate) * avg_loss). Apply half-Kelly cap from config. Return kelly_pct, expected_value, suggested_risk_amount (as suggestion only, user decides).

Create nas100bot/signals.py - orchestrates edge detection and signal generation. (1) Runs all applicable edges for current market state, (2) computes confluence_score (count of triggered edges), (3) determines direction (LONG/SHORT based on which edges dominate), (4) computes weighted_win_rate across active edges, (5) calls kelly.py for position sizing suggestion, (6) determines time-of-day context (kill zone 9:30-11:00, dead zone 12:00-14:00, etc), (7) sets stop_loss (below PDL for longs, above PDH for shorts), (8) sets targets (PDH for longs, PDL for shorts as draw on liquidity), (9) computes risk:reward ratio. Returns a Signal dataclass with all fields.

Create nas100bot/telegram_bot.py - formats Signal into a readable Telegram message with all quant stats, sends via python-telegram-bot async API. Message format shows: direction, confluence score, edge breakdown, win rate, EV, Kelly %, suggested size (with disclaimer that user decides), stop loss, targets, time context, R:R ratio. Include bold/emoji formatting for Telegram.

Create nas100bot/timing.py - utility module for time-of-day logic: is_kill_zone(dt) -> bool (9:30-11:00 ET), is_dead_zone(dt) -> bool (12:00-14:00 ET), is_weak_period(dt) -> bool (Thu/Fri 3PM ET), get_best_long_days() -> ['Monday', 'Wednesday'], high_of_day_window() -> '9:30-10:30 ET (43.6%)', low_of_day_window() -> '9:30-10:30 ET (53.4%)'

Create nas100bot/scheduler.py - schedule-based runner: checks at market open (9:30 ET), after first hour (10:30 ET), during kill zone, and at user-configured intervals. Uses schedule library. Only runs on market days (Mon-Fri, skip market holidays).
Create nas100bot/main.py - entry point: loads config, initializes modules, starts scheduler loop. Supports --dry-run flag for testing without Telegram. Includes logging setup (to file + stdout).
Create tests/test_edges.py - unit tests for all edge detection functions with mock data. Test both triggered and not-triggered cases.
Create tests/test_kelly.py - unit tests for Kelly criterion calculations with known values.
Create tests/test_signals.py - unit tests for signal generation with mocked edge results.
Create tests/test_timing.py - unit tests for timing utilities (kill zone, dead zone, weak period detection).
Create tests/conftest.py - shared pytest fixtures (mock market data, sample configs).

Create README.md - comprehensive documentation: overview (signal-only system disclaimer), features, setup instructions, configuration guide, how signals work, edge explanations with stats, Kelly criterion explanation, running the bot, architecture diagram (text-based).
acceptance_criteria: python -m pytest tests/ -v passes all tests
python -m nas100bot.main --dry-run runs without errors and logs a startup message
config.example.yaml contains all required settings with documentation comments
README.md clearly states this is SIGNAL-ONLY and user decides all trade execution and sizing
All edge functions return correct win rates matching the research data
Kelly criterion calculation is mathematically correct
Telegram message format includes all required fields: direction, confluence, edges, win rate, EV, Kelly %, suggested size, stop loss, targets, time context, R:R
Code never auto-executes trades or auto-determines position sizes without user confirmation
verification: Run: pip install -r requirements.txt (confirm no errors)
Run: python -m pytest tests/ -v (confirm all tests pass)
Run: python -m nas100bot.main --dry-run (confirm it starts, logs, and exits cleanly)
findings: All 122 tests pass. Dry-run mode works correctly, fetching real market data from yfinance and evaluating all edges. Fixed numpy boolean type issue (np.True_ vs Python True) by explicitly casting to bool() in edge functions that do pandas/numpy comparisons. Used python3 command as python is not aliased in this pyenv setup.
